[b-t] How do these compare with the recently posted Flashforge printers?
I just bought a Creator Pro 5, and it arrived today, still in box…
[Yer] Bambu doesn’t have an affordable multi tool head solution so the creator 5 is great for saving on poop when you’re doing multi coloured printing.
[sky42856] Have had my CPro5 for a month now. Print quality is comparable to my P1S. It offers so much more versatile use. Simply put, it does everything that a X2D can do, and even more. I don't print much multi colour but I do multi-filament print , eg PLA+PETG support (vice versa). It also excel in engineering filament with stock hardened nozzles and chamber heater.
Software-wise, it can be improved and it is improving / debugging.
Biggest trade-off is stepping away from the Bambu ecosystem, but you can still use makerworld models through https://forgebridge.app/
[quick-dry] how are you finding the print quality, and the slicer? most of my multi-filament is for support, so the C5Pro is drawing me in over the Snapmaker because of heated chamber and all that out of the box rather than adding a pandabreath or whatever - though closed firmware versus Klipper swings me the other way. My understanding is that Flashforge require their own version of Orca? (current printer is a Sovol, but I need the chamber so it's pensioned off to thins that can go open air printing)
(Most prints are my own stuff, built in F360, so the various online ecosystem things aren't a showstopper)
[3dprintdeals] Nice price on the X2D combo
H3c is being announced on Nov 4. Don't expect it to be cheap
https://www.reddit.com/r/BambuLab/s/mpmRUwEudi
[moltenaus] Nice find, I'm looking forward to seeing what the P3C has to offer for a hopefully more stomachable price.
[letmethefuqin] Looking to buy my first 3d printer
Don’t really know what I want to print other than little nick nacks,
Which of the above should I look at
[moltenaus] I can highly recommend picking up a Bambu A1, it's an incredibly reliable printer and the quality is amazing, doubly so for the price. I started with a Bambu P2S 4 months ago, then picked up an A1 last month and have since sold my P2S that was three times the price of the A1. It's also 'cheap' enough that even if you don't stick with it you're not that much out of pocket. You won't be able to print engineering filaments though, so that is something to consider.
I would also recommend getting one from a local seller for local support if something goes wrong.
[hotori] Is the combo worth it or should I stick with the A1 without the combo parts
[jstris] ive read the a1 combo is more than enough and is good value
[pq8382] At current stage get a1 you wont regret. Dont bother p2s or x2d because p3 is on the horizon and its likely more capable than these two. Also all bambu 1st gen machine are rock solid, i have my a1 running for more than 2.5k hours printing without any maintenance and it still run smooth as hell. For my x2d… i did three replacement in first 2 week and finally get a good quality machine, also you need tweak the printng profile yourself for x2d due to poor default settingfor petg type filament. If your pefer some model with high dimension, you may want to consider p1s, this machine is bit old and does not come with touch screen, but default profile is rock solid and you dont need tweak much and you able to get excellent print result in any size
[Blitzfx] I do a lot of 3D printing for work, and I would strongly recommend you just pick up the A1 mini and nothing else. Maybe the combo if you can foresee yourself making colourful / multi-colour prints.
If you don't really know what to print, then you may run into the risk of having the printer as dead weight after 1 year because you don't know what to print with it or got bored with it, so that's why I recommend the cheapest. The risk is lowest, and if you find yourself needing more in the future, then you can just sell it and upgrade, or you can keep it and buy another (I have three different printers)
I have A1 mini and it does literally everything I need to print, but maybe your case may change in the future.
If you are thinking of printing maybe vases, boxes, storage containers, large dragon models, firearms etc. then get the A1 just for a bigger print bed.
[ddoraaaaa] bought my p2s exactly 2 days before x2d drop.. feelbadman

There wasn't any urgency, could have waited for X2D. Still figuring things out in Fusion.
